title: Empathy-line: Sales-Eng Demo Annotated Slides (draft)
body:
Slide 1 — One-sentence opener
Title: Why this demo matters (30s open)
Speaker note: Start with a tiny story — customer A had a live chat feature that dropped at 40% traffic; we helped them keep latency under SLO and cut per-session token cost by 3x. Say it like you observed it in the wild.

Slide 2 — The ‘empathy line’
Title: If you’re tired of unpredictable inference costs and surprise latency spikes…
Speaker note: Pause. Look at the engineer and platform lead faces. The empathy line is designed to make an emotional match before diving technical. Don’t jump to features; affirm the pain. Follow-up lines: “...and you’ve built a prototype that works at low scale but starts losing p99 when traffic spikes” and “...you need predictable capacity without re-architecting infra.”

Slide 3 — Quick trust path (what we’ll prove in 8 minutes)
Bullets: 1) Consistent p95/p99 under mixed traffic, 2) How routing + cache reduces token volume by 30–60% for typical sessions, 3) Fallback plan so app stays online on overload.
Speaker note: Set expectations: this is not a model-race. It’s about serving reliably at product scale. Use measured language: "we’ll show operational levers".

Slide 4 — Live topology sketch (diagram)
Title: Request flow: App -> Redwood Gateway -> Routing -> Host Pool (cached) -> Fallback variant
Speaker note: Walk slowly. Call out the 3 decision points where you can save cost or preserve latency: routing policy, KV/prefix cache, quantized variant fallback. Bring up a one-sentence cost impact for each.

Slide 5 — Field cue: quick questions to ask the buyer
List: "What latency SLO matter most?", "How predictable is your session length?", "Do you have hard compliance regions?"
Speaker note: Use these to steer. If they say "SLO = 250ms p95" immediately offer the small-config suggestion (dedicated pool pinned + autoscale headroom).

Slide 6 — Short demo plan (2 phases)
Phase A: Baseline (unoptimized) — show increased tail latency on burst;
Phase B: Apply 3 levers (routing rule, KV prefix caching, model variant) and show recovery.
Speaker note: Keep Phase A short (70–90s). The goal is to make the improvement obvious. Use numbers, not adjectives.

Slide 7 — Live CLI snippets to run (annotated)
Code lines shown in slides (example):
- redwood api serve --model open-7b --route default
- redwood routing create --policy latency-first --fallback open-3b-q4
- redwood cache enable --prefix session:ctx --ttl 120s
Speaker note: Narrate what each command is doing in one sentence; don’t try to teach CLI to the buyer. If buyer is non-technical, skip to the effect (latency/cost delta).

Slide 8 — Before/after numbers (synthesized small table)
Rows: p95 latency, p99 latency, tokens per session, cost per 1k sessions
Before: 420ms, 890ms, 6.2k tokens, $12.40
After: 220ms, 300ms, 2.8k tokens, $4.10
Speaker note: Flag assumptions: batch size distribution, median session length, prompt templating ratio. Say "these are representative; we’ll run your traces in follow-up."

Slide 9 — Quick fallback script (ops play)
Title: If a canary blips during pilot
Bullets: 1) Redirect 20% to fallback model, 2) Pause autoscale down triggers, 3) Increase cache TTL for hot sessions, 4) Open incident chat with Redwood SE (seed template in linked artifacts).
Speaker note: This is the reassure step — buyers want to know they won’t lose customers mid-pilot. Repeat the 20% number; it’s easier to remember than percentages like 17%.

Slide 10 — Objection playbook (rapid responses)
Objection: "We can’t trust an external service with PII"
Response: "We offer Private (VPC/on-prem) with audit logs and KMS/HSM support; we can run the pilot inside your network or with redaction hooks."

Objection: "We already use provider X and are happy"
Response: "Totally fair — we don’t ask you to rip-and-replace. For pilots we focus on one high-value route and a canary to measure unit economics objectively."

Objection: "How do you guarantee p99?"
Response: "We don’t guarantee without SLA contract. For pilots we instrument and set SLOs; then we recommend the smallest Dedicated pool and routing policy that meets your p99 target."

Slide 11 — Pilot success criteria (quick checklist)
Checklist items: "p95 <= agreed SLO", "token cost improvement >= 30% in production traces", "no dropped requests during peak test", "runbook validated with on-call"
Speaker note: Offer to bake these into the pilot statement of work; buyers like measurable exits.

Slide 12 — Rehearsal script (two-minute roleplay)
Role A (Seller): deliver empathy line, ask one qualifying question, demo Phase A (45s), apply levers (45s), call for decision (30s).
Role B (Buyer): push on cost, ask about PII, demand p99 number.
Speaker note: Encourage the SE to keep the pace brisk. Use this script in internal dry runs.

Slide 13 — Internal cues for SEs (checkbox before call)
- Do we have customer traces? (Y/N)
- Known SLOs? (Y/N)
- Regulatory constraints? (GDPR/PCI/SO X?)
- Point of contact for infra changes?
Speaker note: If traces are missing, ask to get them post-call; don’t stall the first demo.

Slide 14 — Post-demo follow-up template (email + attachments)
Subject: "Pilot next steps + short replay"
Body bullets: Thank you, attached: replay, baseline metrics, recommended config (+cost delta), proposed pilot SOW (2 weeks), ask for traces if absent.
Speaker note: Keep follow-up within 24 hours. Attach the before/after table and a 1-page SOW.

Slide 15 — Open questions & TODOs
List: "Should we add a variant for high-throughput caching examples?" "Do we surface dedicated pool pricing tiers on slide 8?" "Get legal approval for private deployment checklist."
Speaker note: This is intentionally granular. Mark owners in the slide notes when you finalize.

Appendix — Quick metrics references (single-line citations)
- Typical session token mix (prompt: 40%, system: 20%, user-turns: 40%)
- Cost delta sources: batching, cache saving, quantized model unit price

Notes to self (messy):
- Keep language simple for non-engineers.
- Have a 60s alternative: 1 slide empathy + 1 slide topology + 1 slide numbers + ask for pilot.
- Add two commercial lines: "pilot credits" and "SLA bump for dedicated" to the close.

End of deck.

Version history: draft 0.1 — empathy-driven structure; 0.2 will add live demo checklist and final SOW template.
